page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 server family. It is built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a large 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 64 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, which is designed to support memory-intensive applications.

For storage, the E8ds_v7 includes 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. The underlying Intel architecture provides advanced hardware capabilities, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations. Cryptographic acceleration is also supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, achieving 35.21 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.51 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches an average of 56.24 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show an average of 670.08 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 85.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations perform at average levels, with Redis SET operations handling 15.64 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaching 16.08 GB/sec.

The E8ds_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without the need to scale up to higher vCPU tiers. This resource balance makes the server highly suitable for relational database hosting, in-memory caching systems, data analytics, and medium-scale web serving applications.
